windowTitle: Serial integration stage 11.5 - the launch Gateway key owner and the first model configuration predecessor

necessity.decision: docs/spec/target/06_data_flow_and_state_machine.md F08 rows 6 and 8 place gateway CreateManagedKey and fabric BindSecret on the Workspace owner at launch; docs/decisions.md and docs/invariants.md make Gateway the sole key issuer and forbid Serve from minting a Gateway key. The merged F09 replacement contract (44d754fe) requires the first UpdateWorkspaceModels to name the exact active predecessor binding.
necessity.currentProblem: Serve.Deploy minted the launch Gateway key and bound its Secret inside Serve (resolveManagedKeyBinding), so the launch-established fabric.secret_bindings id was never recorded where the Workspace could read it. A runtime whose revision declares the installation Gateway credential therefore had no predecessor available to the first UpdateWorkspaceModels: the update called Fabric BindSecret for an already-bound runtime purpose and Fabric refused the different Secret with AlreadyExists, so the first model configuration could never be applied on either product combination. The launch also omitted the workspace->gateway CreateManagedKey and workspace->fabric BindSecret continuations the SSOT names for F08.
confirmedFacts: docs/spec/target/06_data_flow_and_state_machine.md F08 row 6 is workspace->gateway GatewayCoordination.CreateManagedKey and row 8 is runtime_control->fabric FabricCoordination.BindSecret; F09 row 4/5 repeat them on the Workspace owner for the update
services/serve/internal/delivery/secret.go resolveManagedKeyBinding called s.Gateway.CreateManagedKey inside Serve's Deploy, which the Gateway owner admits only to the Workspace peer
RuntimeDeployCommand already carries RuntimeManagedKeyBinding managed_key_binding = 17 and the Workspace order result already persists an orderResult the launch and update paths both decode
a focused test before this change proved the collision: a launch-established binding made the first UpdateWorkspaceModels reach Fabric BindSecret and be refused with AlreadyExists
necessity.outcome: Workspace resumeRuntime now issues and binds the launch key before Deploy and freezes the binding on the command and the order result; activeModelSecretBindingID falls back to that launch binding as the first configuration's predecessor; revokeSupersededKey revokes the launch key after Serve confirms the new version; and Serve resolveManagedKeyBinding applies the Workspace-issued binding or refuses, never minting one.

ssotConformance.requirement: rows 6 and 8: Workspace calls GatewayCoordination.CreateManagedKey and then FabricCoordination.BindSecret at launch, before Serve Deploy.
ssotConformance.conformance: Workspace resumeRuntime calls CreateManagedKey and BindSecret before Deploy and records the opaque binding; Serve Deploy no longer mints or binds.

ssotConformance.requirement: the first configuration replaces the launch binding through RebindSecret with the expected predecessor.
ssotConformance.conformance: activeModelSecretBindingID returns the launch binding id when no model-configuration update has succeeded, so the first update names it as the RebindSecret predecessor.

ssotConformance.requirement: Gateway Integration is the sole writer and issuer of a Workspace-managed Gateway key; Serve is not a Gateway-key writer.
ssotConformance.conformance: Serve resolveManagedKeyBinding contains no Gateway or Fabric call; it validates and applies the Workspace-issued binding only.

focused.covers: ensureRuntimeGatewayBinding issues/binds the launch key once and reuses the recorded binding on restart, mints nothing without a declared credential, the first update rebinds against the launch predecessor and revokes the launch key, plus all existing launch/model tests.
Deploy applies the Workspace-issued binding and mints/binds nothing; a missing or incomplete binding is refused before the deployment becomes active; the reload path still mints nothing.
BindSecret initial-bind/replay and RebindSecret predecessor CAS are unchanged.
the Workspace accepted-operation grant still admits the Gateway and Fabric audiences.

claimBoundary: Source-check and focused owner tests only. This proves the launch key now travels the SSOT owner path and that the first model configuration can name a real predecessor. It does not prove a Candidate exists, an Instance deployed, a Tencent resource was provisioned, or either product combination is accepted end to end.
